title: Machine Learning Tool for Automated Analysis of Electron Microscopy Images
content: Accurate characterization of nanomaterials is essential for ensuring quality control and reliability in manufacturing industries that depend on advanced materials. Electron microscopy techniques such as transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) serve as crucial techniques in nanomaterial analysis, yet manual analysis of such images remains time-intensive and subject to human variability. Recent advances in machine learning (ML) have demonstrated the potential of deep learning models to automate and enhance image-based material characterization. We have developed an AI-powered material characterization tool utilizing deep learning techniques to enhance precision and efficiency in identifying materials in TEM and SEM images. Our approach employs the state-of-the-art convolutional neural networks (CNNs) trained on labeled EM datasets, integrating active learning methodologies to iteratively refine and improve model predictions. The system aims to automate material classification and extract essential metrics such as purity, size, and shape distribution, thereby accelerating the material characterization workflow.
